accepted.name: INvets
accepted.description: Statewide Indiana nonprofit founded by veterans that helps transitioning service members, veterans, Guard/Reserve, and military spouses find meaningful civilian careers and connect to community resources across Indiana.
accepted.eligibility: U.S. veterans, transitioning service members, Guard/Reserve, and military spouses.

accepted.name: Indy Honor Flight
accepted.description: Indianapolis-based Honor Flight hub providing all-expenses-paid trips to Washington, D.C., for veterans to visit their memorials, with volunteer guardians and a mission to honor veterans for their service.
accepted.cost: Free to veterans; guardians pay their own way or are sponsored
accepted.geographicScope: Indiana (primarily central Indiana; serves veterans across the state)
accepted.eligibility: Veterans of World War II, Korean War, Vietnam War, and terminally ill veterans from any era (as stated on site).
accepted.availability: Trips scheduled seasonally; applications accepted year-round.

accepted.name: Military Assistance Mission (MAM)
accepted.description: Indiana-based nonprofit providing emergency financial assistance grants to active-duty military, Guard/Reserve, veterans, and their families facing short-term financial hardship to help cover basic needs like housing, utilities, food, and transportation.
accepted.eligibility: Active-duty military, Guard/Reserve, veterans, or their families in Indiana experiencing a short-term financial crisis.

accepted.name: HVAF of Indiana
accepted.description: Indianapolis-based nonprofit serving veterans experiencing homelessness or housing instability by providing housing, employment services, case management, and basic needs support throughout central Indiana.
accepted.geographicScope: Central Indiana (Indianapolis metro and surrounding areas)
accepted.eligibility: U.S. veterans experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness.

accepted.name: Indiana Warrior Partnership
accepted.description: Statewide Indiana program connecting veterans and their families with community-based resources, care coordination, and support services to address employment, education, housing, health, and wellness needs.
accepted.eligibility: Veterans, transitioning service members, Guard/Reserve, and their families in Indiana.

accepted.name: Indiana Gold Star Families
accepted.description: Indiana-based nonprofit supporting families of fallen service members through community events, peer connection, remembrance activities, and assistance navigating resources available to Gold Star Families.
accepted.eligibility: Families of service members who died in the line of duty or as a result of military service.

accepted.name: The Hundred Club of Indiana
accepted.description: Indiana nonprofit providing financial assistance, scholarships, and support to the families of law enforcement officers, firefighters, EMS, and corrections officers who have died or been catastrophically injured in the line of duty.
accepted.eligibility: Families of Indiana first responders killed or catastrophically injured in the line of duty.

accepted.name: Indiana Fallen Heroes Foundation
accepted.description: Indiana-based nonprofit honoring and supporting fallen public safety officers and their families by providing financial assistance, scholarships, and remembrance events for families of law enforcement, fire, EMS, and corrections personnel.
accepted.eligibility: Families of Indiana public safety officers who died in the line of duty.
accepted.availability: Applications reviewed as received; support provided based on stated eligibility.

accepted.name: Hoosier Burn Camp
accepted.description: Indiana nonprofit providing a week-long summer camp experience for children ages 8–18 who have experienced burn injuries, along with year-round activities designed to build confidence, connection, and support for campers and their families.
accepted.eligibility: Children ages 8–18 in Indiana who have sustained a burn injury.

accepted.name: Guardian Revival
accepted.description: Indiana-based nonprofit providing confidential, trauma-informed mental health retreats and peer support programs specifically designed for first responders, including law enforcement, fire, EMS, dispatch, corrections, and healthcare workers.
accepted.cost: Free to participants (retreats and programming are donor-funded)
accepted.eligibility: Active or retired first responders (law enforcement, fire, EMS, dispatch, corrections, healthcare).
